summary: When Nora speaks into a quiet room unprompted, she now remembers the people in it.
details: The participation turn — the one where nobody called her and the room simply went quiet — used to read nothing at all from memory. It knew who was talking by display name and no more, because that turn is held on nobody's behalf and every memory block she has was keyed to whoever had tagged her.

It now carries two blocks: what she said or did before (`<self_card>`), and what she has concluded about each person who spoke in the window (`<people_in_window>`). Both are curated to what the room is actually talking about, and both are marked as a record of the past she may be wrong about and may contradict — never as something anybody just said to her, and never as an instruction.

The practical difference: a room that has taken to calling her 管理員 as a joke can say «麻煩管理員處理一下» without tagging her, and she can know it means her. A room with no such history gets silence, which is the right answer there.

The once-a-day proactive pass's roster now carries one remembered line per member beside each name, so the two memory lookups it is allowed per pass are spent on depth instead of on working out who these people are.
limitations: Bounded: up to 4 speakers and 3 conclusions each on a participation turn, and 1 conclusion for each of up to 12 home-room members on the proactive pass. A window with more speakers than that shows the ones talking most recently.

Those bounds are settings under `[memory]`, but they are DEFAULTS, not an opt-in: a deployment that says nothing about them gets the new blocks on at 4 x 3 the next time it restarts, which is up to four extra memory lookups on a participation turn. Set any of them to 0 to turn a block off.
Only people the deployment's identity file maps. An unmapped sender contributes nothing, because there is no memory filed under a raw phone number.

The cheap gate in front of the participation turn is unchanged and still sees only the transcript and Nora's own position in the room — by design, so that what she remembers can never be what decides she is allowed to speak.
Memory being unreachable costs the block and never the turn: she speaks or stays silent on whatever else is in front of her.
